the bacterial flagellium, a well‐studied motility organelle, is a sensor that regulates its own biogenesis as well as that of other physiological functions, such as the type three secretion system.
the flagellum is a sensor that detects external wetness and that the flagellin export pathway is the signal transducer.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that flagella play in bacterial physiology and behavior.
the role of the bacterial flagellin protein in sensing the external hydration of the environment.
the role of bacterial flagella in sensing the external wetness environment and in modulating gene expression in response to this stimulus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the flagellum is a multifunctional organelle that is involved in motility as well as chemotaxis, and that the flagellin protein is a multifunction protein that is involved in both motility and chemotaxis.
the flagellar system in Salmonella is a sensor of environmental conditions that can affect the biogenesis of the flagellum and also the secretion of other proteins.
the flagellum is a sensor of external wetness and that it couples the flagellar motor and the TTSS to external wetness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the flagellum is not just a motility organ, but a sensory organ as well.
we have uncovered a new function for the flagellum in the sensing of external wetness, which in turn affects the expression of genes associated with motility and virulence.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the flagellum has an important role in sensing external wetting, a role distinct from its function in motility, chemotaxis and biofilm formation.
the bacterial flagellin filament is an environmental sensor, and that the flagellum is coupled to the type three secretion system of Salmonella.
